study: PhysX wheel contact and nonlinear tire laws for large-angle turning
systems: Unscaled simulated CARLA traj_4 source and explicitly assumed four-wheel FWD surrogate
Existing TRON1 WF driven two-wheel articulation

main_law_comparison.geometry: same authored cylinder and native normal contact within each system

single_wheel_completed_protocol_amendmen.angular_fixture_locks: worldX/Z only, all XYZ translation free

car.interpretation: Record contact losses, rollover and path divergence as surrogate outcomes; do not rank tire accuracy or claim exact source reproduction.
car.Vehicle_SDK_separate_arm: Adds native suspension/road queries/default Vehicle tire model. This changes more than the tangent curve and cannot be pooled into the matched-geometry law ablation.

measurements.body_beta: worldXY velocity course minus projected body-forward heading
measurements.wheel_side_angle: each wheel COM velocity relative to its axle/world-up rolling plane
measurements.patch_slip: COM velocity plus angular velocity cross measured contact-point offset
measurements.external_tangent_force: recorded applied world force, paired separately with used lagged load and next measured load
measurements.aggregate_force_utilization: horizontal tangent force norm divided by mu times vertical normal load; only load>5N

scale_caution.steady_turn_lean_illustration: tan(lean) approximately lateral_acceleration/g, under a flat-floor centroidal steady-turn approximation; not a prescribed trunk angle or absolute-height target

render.layout: four horizontal panels: reference and three recorded law arms
render.camera: fixed world orthographic XY bounds, no zoom, yaw follow, alignment or smoothing
